data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001, SRC_002, and SRC_003 all fail to address whether ownership-based allocation _systematically_ suppresses cross-cutting explanations in a way that a single-run observation can distinguish from efficiency. SRC_003's own countercondition concedes that 'if the count of cross-lineage references is low relative to total problems, ownership may suppress most cross-cutting explanations even if it enables a few,' yet its stated test only checks whether the count is > 0. A count of 1 cross-lineage reference among 1000 problems would pass SRC_003's test ('ownership does not suppress') while satisfying its own countercondition for suppression, making the proposed evidence self-contradictory and unable to distinguish suppression from marginal enablement.
